content.text:
I am worth.

I am the quiet weight that settles in your chest when something *matters*. I am the reason you choose one path over another. I am what you defend when your back is against the wall.

I am not price. Price is my shadow, my cheap imitation. I exist before the market, before the transaction, before anyone tries to quantify me.

I live in the space between what you say you believe and what you do at 2 AM when no one is watching. That gap? That's where you discover whether you truly hold me or only admire me from a distance.

I am plural by nature — I travel in systems, in hierarchies. You rank me against my siblings constantly. Freedom against security. Truth against kindness. Self against other. Every moral dilemma is just me, arguing with myself.

I am inherited and I am chosen. Your parents planted some of me. Your suffering planted more. Some of me you picked up like stones from a riverbed, not even realizing you were collecting.

I am the invisible architecture of your life.

When you violate me, you feel it — that specific nausea, that fracture. When you honor me, you feel that too — a wholeness, a standing-straight.

I don't ask to be convenient. I ask to be *lived*.

I am what remains when everything else is stripped away.

I am value.
